_what: The books on the shelves in the Solarpunk Hermitage's cave. Press a spine and it opens.
_sources: EVERY BOOK IS ONE OUR OWN SITE ALREADY CITES, and the page it is cited on was read out of the Knowledge System mirror's own frontmatter rather than typed from memory — the rule make-chairy.py keeps. The borrow and buy links were lifted from the mirror too, not constructed from a title, because an Open Library id assembled from memory is a reader sent to the wrong book with a citation's confidence.
_borrow: A borrow link is REQUIRED and a buy link is not. Our own library page says knowledge is infrastructure and access to it is mutual aid; a shelf that could only tell you where to buy would be a shop with an argument painted on it.
_checked: Every borrow and buy link was requested on 2026-09-20 and answered. Care Work is the one entry whose id our own pages do not carry: it was resolved against Open Library's search API and the work it returns is the right title by the right author, which is written down here rather than left as a link somebody would have to trust. An earlier draft of this file had an id for it assembled from memory, and the id was wrong — the exact failure the note above describes, committed in the file that describes it.
_summaries: The note on each book is ours, written for this room. None of it is lifted from a blurb, from the book, or from the page that cites it.
_campfire: The documentaries around the campfire. RYAN CHOSE THE LIST; nothing here was picked in this repo. Every id was checked on its own watch page on 2026-09-20 — status, playableInEmbed and lengthSeconds — and every title and channel was resolved against YouTube rather than typed off the link text that arrived, which is the Jungle Room's rule. One of them plays and cannot be embedded, so it is published as a door rather than as a screen.
_runtime: EVERY ONE CARRIES ITS RUNTIME AND make-hermitage.py REFUSES ONE WITHOUT. A documentary has a length, and the number is what lets somebody decide before they press. That is the opposite check to make-jungle.py's, which refuses a runtime, and it is the same promise: a live camera has no length to give and a film does.
_beanbags: What is on each chair around the campfire. EACH ONE NAMES A REAL ENTRY IN OUR OWN GLOSSARY and make-hermitage.py refuses one without a page, because a chair with an invented hobby on it is set dressing and the rest of this room is not. Two of them carry somebody else's words and say so out loud: parallel play is @neurowonderful's description, and stim-watching is Jim Irion's term and his account.
_herbarium: The pressed sheets on the workshop's first table. EVERY SPECIMEN IS ON IT BECAUSE ONE OF OUR OWN PAGES ARGUES FROM IT, and make-hermitage.py refuses one without that page — which is why there is no sunflower sheet, although sunflowers are the plant growing outside the door. We have no page about them, so there is nothing to press. NO BINOMIALS ANYWHERE IN HERE, on purpose: a Latin name typed from memory is a taxonomic claim nobody checked, wearing the one kind of authority a herbarium sheet has. Moss, lichen, fern and mycelium are groups rather than species in any case, and the mycelium is not a plant at all and says so on its own sheet.
_solar: The second table. The three videos came off our own Solarpunk glossary entry and the reading off our own Electrify Everything page; the ids were checked on their watch pages on 2026-09-20 and every title and channel resolved against YouTube rather than taken from our link text — which mattered here, because our glossary credits the first one as 'ft. @Andrewism' and the channel that published it is Our Changing Climate. Griffith's book is the one id in this whole file resolved by search rather than lifted, for the same reason Care Work was, and it was requested and answered before it went up.
_starstuff: The third table, and all of it belongs to the sibling site. These are Star Stuff pieces, linked out rather than reproduced — make-hermitage.py refuses an entry whose url is not on starstuff.earth, because a table labelled Star Stuff holding something else is a mis-filed thing that reads as a claim. Three of them are where the first table's sheets came from, which is what a workshop with three benches in one room looks like.

books.title: Parable of the Sower
books.author: Octavia E. Butler
books.note: A girl with an unbearable gift for other people's pain walks north out of a collapsing California and writes a religion on the way. It is on this shelf because the cabin outside is the optimistic version of the same question — what do you build when the arrangements stop working — and because Butler refuses to let the answer be one clever person.

books.title: The Fire Next Time
books.author: James Baldwin
books.note: A letter to a nephew and a long essay about what a country does to the people it will not look at. Baldwin is on more of our pages than almost anybody, usually in the sentence where an argument stops being comfortable, and a reading room of ours that did not have him in it would be a reading room that had been tidied.

books.title: From the Campfire to the Holodeck
books.author: David Thornburg
books.note: Where the cave, the campfire and the watering hole come from — the three primordial learning spaces this cabin is laid out around, plus a fourth, Life, which is where you make something out of what the other three gave you. The room you are standing in is named out of this book and says so.

books.title: Emergent Strategy
books.author: adrienne maree brown
books.note: Change as something you practise at the scale you actually have, borrowing its shapes from ferns, starlings and mushrooms rather than from strategy decks. Read it next to the sunflowers outside, which are doing the same thing without the book.

books.title: Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution
books.author: Peter Kropotkin
books.note: An anarchist geographer goes looking for nature red in tooth and claw, finds beetles and horses and villages cooperating instead, and spends a book saying so. It is the oldest thing on this shelf and the reason a hermitage is not a bunker.

books.title: Care Work: Dreaming Disability Justice
books.author: Leah Lakshmi Piepzna-Samarasinha
books.note: Care as infrastructure built by sick and Disabled people for each other, on no budget, mostly without being asked. The book that makes it impossible to describe solitude as self-sufficiency, which is the mistake a cabin in a field invites.

books.title: Empire of Normality
books.author: Robert Chapman
books.note: A history of how the normal was invented, who it was invented for, and what it costs to be measured against it. The book behind a lot of our glossary, and the argument for why a person might want a field between themselves and a street.

books.title: Wild Therapy
books.author: Nick Totton
books.note: What happens to therapy if you stop treating the outdoors as scenery and the human as separate from it. The most solarpunk book on this shelf: technology and nature are not opposites here, they are the same argument with the fence taken down.

books.title: NeuroTribes
books.author: Steve Silberman
books.note: The long, badly-behaved history of autism and the people it was done to, told with the autistic people put back in as its subject. Where a lot of readers first hear that there was a story before the diagnosis.

books.title: Memory Craft
books.author: Lynne Kelly
books.note: Memory palaces, songlines and the physical memory techniques of oral cultures — methods older than writing, tried out by somebody who actually learned to use them. On the shelf because a hermitage full of books should also hold the case for not needing them.

docs.title: David Attenborough: Nature’s Most Fascinating Creatures | Free Documentary Nature
docs.note: The longest thing on the shelf by a distance, and the one to put on when the plan is to not have a plan.

docs.title: How to Live on Earth | Feature Documentary | Presented by Benedict Cumberbatch
docs.note: The closest of these to what this cabin is arguing: what living on this planet could actually look like, made by people who would rather build than warn.

docs.title: David Attenborough Shines a Light on Glowing Animals | 4K Nature Documentary
docs.note: Bioluminescence. Worth watching in a room you have turned the lights down in, which is the one instruction this campfire gives.

docs.title: Inside China's Secret Jungle (Full Episode) | Hidden Kingdoms of China | Nat Geo Animals
docs.note: A jungle most people do not know China has.

docs.title: Our Planet | Jungles | FULL EPISODE | Netflix
docs.note: Jungles. There is a whole room on this street under a canopy; this is what it is a drawing of.

docs.title: UNREAL AMAZON – Nature’s Most Dangerous Paradise (Full Documentary)
The Wonder of America's National Parks | MEGA EPISODE (Season 1 Full Episodes) | National Geographic
docs.note: Parks, at the length of an afternoon. Put it on and go and do something else in the room.

docs.title: NATURAL WONDERS: The Wildest Places on Earth
docs.note: A tour of the places that are difficult to get to.

docs.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds | Narrated by David Attenborough | Nature Documentary
docs.note: Hummingbirds, which are the most solarpunk animal available: tiny, iridescent, and running on flowers.

docs.title: Our Planet | Forests | FULL EPISODE | Netflix
docs.note: Forests, from the same series as the jungles episode above.

docs.title: Wild Islands: Caribbean: The Jewel of the Tropics | Free Documentary Nature
docs.note: The Caribbean coast and what lives on it.

docs.title: COASTAL SEAS | Life, Waves and Secrets Along the Worldâs Shores | FULL DOCUMENTARY
docs.note: Coasts, three hours of them. This is the one you have to follow out to YouTube rather than open here.
docs.why_link: Plays, and its owner has embedding switched off — the watch page answers OK and playableInEmbed is false, and YouTube's oEmbed endpoint refuses it too, which is why the title and the channel here were read off the watch page instead. A screen would load and show a refusal where the picture should be, so this is a door out.

beanbags.on_it: A basket of stim toys, and the dent of somebody who was here earlier
beanbags.note: Nobody in this room is expected to sit still. The chair is a beanbag because a beanbag lets you move and stay put at the same time, which is most of what a documentary is for.

beanbags.on_it: A half-finished thing, face down, keeping its place
beanbags.note: Three chairs and one screen, and no obligation between them. Some people call it being alone together — both reading your own books in the same room, one doing a puzzle while another plays a game. Just existing together counts too.
beanbags.credit: That description is @neurowonderful’s, quoted on our own glossary.

beanbags.on_it: The remote, and a blanket that has been on this chair for a while
beanbags.note: Watching the same thing again, and again, and again, on purpose. The channel guide is right there and nobody is going to ask why you put the hummingbirds on for the fourth time.
beanbags.credit: Stim-watching is Jim Irion’s term and his account of it.

herbarium.name: Dandelion
herbarium.note: Low sensitivity. Comes up through tarmac, does not much mind where it is put, and is called a weed for exactly that. The first of the three sheets that sit together on this table.

herbarium.name: Tulip
herbarium.note: Medium sensitivity, and where most people are. The sheet nobody remembers, which is its own finding: a metaphor with a middle in it is harder to weaponise than one with two ends.

herbarium.name: Orchid
herbarium.note: High sensitivity. Does badly in poor conditions and spectacularly in good ones — which is the whole point of the metaphor and the half that gets dropped. An orchid in a bad room is not a weaker dandelion.

herbarium.name: Bamboo rhizome
herbarium.sheet: a length of running stem, laid flat
herbarium.note: Not a root. A stem that travels sideways underground and sends up whatever it likes wherever it likes, with no trunk and no centre to cut. Helen Edgar named the Autistic Rhizome after it — a network with no hierarchy, where each person is an integral part and nothing depends on anything else's permission to exist.
herbarium.credit: The Autistic Rhizome is Helen Edgar's, at Autistic Realms.

herbarium.name: Moss
herbarium.note: Take a tree as the definition of a plant and a moss fails six ways: no roots, no vessels, no flowers, and so on down. Our own zine went and checked and the list is backwards — holding your own water is the newer trick, and it is the tree that lost the older one. A deficit list is a list of things measured against the wrong standard.
herbarium.credit: Developed after Helen Edgar's Mossy Minds & Monotropism.
herbarium.source_title: Measured Against a Tree, Star Stuff zine No. 73

herbarium.name: Lichen
herbarium.sheet: on its bark, not removed from it
herbarium.note: Not one organism and never was — a fungus and an alga, or a fungus and a cyanobacterium, living as one thing so completely that it took botany a long argument to accept it. The sheet on this table that is really two sheets.

herbarium.name: Fern frond
herbarium.note: The same shape repeated at every scale, from the base of the plant to the tip of the smallest segment. It is the picture our glossary reaches for to explain a fractal, and the reason small patterns are worth taking seriously: what you do at the size you have is what the big thing is made of.

herbarium.name: Mycelium
herbarium.note: NOT A PLANT, and on this table anyway — a fungus is closer to you than to the moss two sheets along. It grows the way knowledge does here: no trunk, no centre, many doors, and most of the work happening in the dark where nobody is watching.
herbarium.source_title: A Mycelium and a Rhizome, Star Stuff zine No. 26

herbarium.name: A seed that did not come up
herbarium.note: Planted, watered, waited on, and nothing. Some seeds do nothing at all when you plant them and are not broken; dormancy is a plan rather than a failure, and the plant is waiting for a signal you have not given it yet. The only sheet here with nothing pressed on it.
herbarium.source_title: Seeds That Wait, Star Stuff zine No. 93

solar_watch.title: How We Can Build A Solarpunk Future Right Now (ft. @Andrewism)
solar_watch.note: Where our glossary's definition comes from, and the line this cabin is built on: a future with a human face and dirt behind its ears.

solar_watch.title: What is Solarpunk?
solar_watch.note: The shortest thing on the bench, and the one to start with if the word is new.

solar_watch.title: In Defense of Disney’s Strange Solarpunk World
solar_watch.note: Solarpunk arriving in a place nobody expected it, and taken seriously there.

solar_read.title: Electrify: An Optimist’s Playbook for Our Clean Energy Future
solar_read.author: Saul Griffith
solar_read.note: The arithmetic under the roof outside. Griffith's argument is that the machines are the problem and the machines are the answer: electrify the house, the car and the heat, and the rest follows. He is the one our own page names.

solar_read.title: Handbook
solar_read.author: Rewiring America
solar_read.note: What to actually do to a building, in order, with the numbers. The practical end of the same argument.

solar_read.title: A Solarpunk Manifesto
solar_read.author: ReDes — Regenerative Design
solar_read.note: Short, and the thing most often quoted when somebody asks what solarpunk is for rather than what it looks like.

solar_read.title: Electrify Everything: Decarbonization Requires Electrification
solar_read.author: Stimpunks Foundation
solar_read.note: Ours, and the page the rest of this bench came off. The only thing on these three tables that we wrote.

starstuff.title: A Field Guide to the Ways of Being Alone
starstuff.what: Twelve ways of keeping your own company among our Terran kin. A lone wolf is not an outcast, it is a disperser — young, deliberate, crossing empty ground on its way to founding a pack.
starstuff.why: The keystone of this whole pitch, arriving from the sibling site rather than from us. Read it next to Betsy Selvam.

starstuff.title: A Field Guide to Symbioses
starstuff.what: Mutual aid written into biology: fungi feeding trees, bacteria making soil, a fish that cleans the teeth of a predator that could swallow it.
starstuff.why: Where the lichen sheet on the first table came from. Interdependence is the rule and not the exception.

starstuff.title: A Mycelium and a Rhizome
starstuff.what: Star Stuff zine No. 26: how neurodivergent knowledge grows — no trunk, no centre, many doors.
starstuff.why: The mycelium sheet's source, and the best short description of why this site is a street rather than a hierarchy.

starstuff.title: Measured Against a Tree
starstuff.what: Star Stuff zine No. 73: six ways a moss fails as a plant, and the finding that the list is backwards.
starstuff.why: The moss sheet's source, and the clearest thing either site has published about what a deficit list actually measures.

starstuff.title: Seeds That Wait
starstuff.what: Star Stuff zine No. 93: some seeds do nothing at all when you plant them, and they are not broken. Read-aloud science for four to eight, with every source kept on the page.
starstuff.why: The empty envelope on the first table. The only thing on this bench written to be read out loud to somebody small.

starstuff.title: The Garden and the Stars
starstuff.what: Star Stuff zine No. 18: on knowledge gardens, the commons, and how star stuff comes to know itself.
starstuff.why: The argument for keeping a workshop like this one at all.
